scenes.label: OIL STAINS ON CONCRETE

scenes.vo: two college dropouts who had barely twenty-five dollars between them,

scenes.vo: and an act of petty corporate theft that almost destroyed their friendship before it even began.

scenes.label: THE SAINT & THE PROPHET
scenes.vo: It was an uneasy partnership between an engineering saint and a ruthless commercial prophet.

scenes.label: VALLEY MISFITS, 1971
scenes.vo: In 1971, Steve Wozniak and Steve Jobs were teenage misfits in the smoggy suburbs of Silicon Valley.

scenes.label: THE ELECTRON DANCE
scenes.vo: Wozniak was a gentle, childlike prodigy who built electronic circuits for the pure, uncorrupted joy of making electrons dance.

scenes.label: REED COLLEGE DROPOUT
scenes.vo: Jobs was a barefoot, brooding wanderer who attended Reed College, dropped out after one semester,

scenes.label: 5-CENT DEPOSIT BOTTLES
scenes.vo: slept on dorm room floors, and returned deposit bottles for five cents to buy food.

scenes.label: ILLEGAL VENTURES
scenes.vo: Their first commercial venture was illegal.

scenes.label: CAP'N CRUNCH WHISTLE
scenes.vo: Wozniak discovered that toy whistles packed inside Cap'n Crunch cereal boxes emitted a tone at exactly twenty-six hundred hertz.

scenes.label: FOOLING THE SWITCHES
scenes.vo: That precise frequency fooled AT&Tâ€™s automated telephone switches into granting free, untraceable long-distance calls across the globe.

scenes.label: THE BLUE BOX
scenes.vo: Woz built an electronic version called a Blue Box.

scenes.label: SELLING FOR $150
scenes.vo: Jobs realized they shouldn't just prank phone companiesâ€”they should sell the boxes to college students for one hundred and fifty dollars each.

scenes.vo: They used one to call the Vatican in Rome, with Wozniak pretending to be Henry Kissinger asking to speak to the Pope in the middle of the night.

scenes.label: THE COLD SHADOW
scenes.vo: Then came the incident that revealed the cold shadow inside Steve Jobs.

scenes.label: ATARI & BREAKOUT
scenes.vo: In 1975, Atari founder Nolan Bushnell hired Jobs to build a single-player version of Pong called Breakout.

scenes.label: THE $700 BASE
scenes.vo: Bushnell offered a bonus: seven hundred dollars for the game,

scenes.label: $100 PER CHIP BOUNTY
scenes.vo: plus an extra one hundred dollars for every computer chip eliminated from the design.

scenes.label: LACKING THE CHOPS
scenes.vo: Jobs knew he lacked the engineering chops to do it,

scenes.label: THE 50/50 PROMISE
scenes.vo: so he begged Wozniak to help, promising they would split the payout fifty-fifty.

scenes.label: FOUR SLEEPLESS NIGHTS
scenes.vo: Wozniak worked for four straight nights without sleep, contracting mono,

scenes.label: 50 CHIPS ELIMINATED
scenes.vo: and designed a masterpiece that cut fifty chips from the circuit board.

scenes.label: THE $5,000 PAYOUT
scenes.vo: Atari paid Jobs a massive five-thousand-dollar bonus.

scenes.label: THE $700 LIE
scenes.vo: Jobs returned to the garage, looked his exhausted best friend in the eye, and told him Atari had paid only seven hundred dollars.

scenes.label: HANDING OVER $350
scenes.vo: He handed Wozniak three hundred and fifty dollars,

scenes.label: POCKETING $4,650
scenes.vo: and pocketed the remaining four thousand six hundred and fifty dollars for himself.

scenes.label: THE TEARS OF WOZ
scenes.vo: Years later, when Wozniak discovered the truth, he broke down and cried.

scenes.label: HE DIDN'T WALK AWAY
scenes.vo: But he didn't walk away.

scenes.label: THE CARDBOARD BOX TRAP
scenes.vo: Because despite Jobsâ€™s ruthless deceit, Woz knew that without Jobs, his brilliant inventions would sit in a cardboard box on a bedroom floor forever.

scenes.label: THE 1976 EPIPHANY
scenes.vo: In early 1976, Wozniak had an epiphany that changed computing history.

scenes.label: MAINFRAME MONSTERS
scenes.vo: At the time, computers were terrifying, multi-million-dollar metal cabinets locked behind plate glass in air-conditioned basements of banks and military installations.

scenes.label: THE WHITE COAT PRIESTHOOD
scenes.vo: They were fed paper punch cards by men in white lab coats.

scenes.label: ABSURDITY IN THE HOME
scenes.vo: The idea that an ordinary human would want a computer in their living room was considered absurd.

scenes.label: KEN OLSEN'S MOCKERY
scenes.vo: Ken Olsen, founder of Digital Equipment Corporation, famously mocked: "There is no reason anyone would want a computer in their home."

scenes.label: WOZNIAK DISAGREED
scenes.vo: Wozniak disagreed.

scenes.label: WIRING ON THE FLOOR
scenes.vo: Sitting on the floor of his cramped apartment, he wired an ordinary keyboard directly to a microprocessor,

scenes.label: THE B&W TV MONITOR
scenes.vo: and hooked the output to a portable black-and-white television screen.

scenes.label: THE KEYPRESS
scenes.vo: He pressed a key.

scenes.label: THE INSTANT LETTER
scenes.vo: And for the first time in human history, the letter appeared instantly on the screen in front of him.

scenes.label: NO PUNCH CARDS
scenes.vo: No punch cards.

scenes.label: NO PRINTOUTS
scenes.vo: No paper printouts.

scenes.label: NO WAITING OVERNIGHT
scenes.vo: No waiting overnight.

scenes.label: PERSONAL COMPUTING BORN
scenes.vo: It was instantaneous, personal computing.

scenes.label: HOMEBREW GYMNASIUM
scenes.vo: Woz was so proud that he took his schematics to the Homebrew Computer Club in Menlo Park

scenes.label: GIVING SCHEMATICS FREE
scenes.vo: and gave them away to fellow hobbyists for free.

scenes.vo: When Jobs saw the machine, he intervened immediately.

scenes.label: STOP GIVING IT AWAY
scenes.vo: "Stop giving it away," Jobs demanded.

scenes.label: BUILD BOARDS AND SELL
scenes.vo: "Let's build circuit boards and sell them."

scenes.label: SELLING THE VW BUS
scenes.vo: To raise the seed capital, Jobs sold his beloved red-and-white Volkswagen microbus for a few hundred dollars.

scenes.label: SELLING THE HP CALCULATOR
scenes.vo: Wozniak sold his prized Hewlett-Packard scientific calculator for five hundred.

scenes.label: $1,300 SEED MONEY
scenes.vo: Combined, they had thirteen hundred dollars.

scenes.vo: They incorporated on April Foolsâ€™ Day, 1976.

scenes.vo: Jobs named it Apple Computer after spending time pruning Gravenstein trees on an Oregon orchard commune.

scenes.label: FRIENDLY & APPROACHABLE
scenes.vo: It sounded friendly, non-threatening,

scenes.vo: Price: five hundred dollars each, cash on delivery.

scenes.vo: Twenty-five thousand dollars.

scenes.label: 30 DAYS PARTS CREDIT
scenes.vo: Jobs badgered electronic suppliers into giving him thirty days of credit on parts.

scenes.label: 50 DELIVERED IN WOOD
scenes.vo: They delivered all fifty computers on time in wooden boxes.

scenes.vo: The Apple I was an underground hit among hardcore hobbyists.

scenes.vo: But Jobs was already dissatisfied.

scenes.label: SIMPLE AS A TOASTER

scenes.vo: Woz sat down and engineered his magnum opus: the Apple II.

scenes.vo: Jobs obsessed over the industrial enclosure.

scenes.vo: Markkula invested ninety-two thousand dollars of his own money,

scenes.vo: secured a quarter-million-dollar line of credit,

scenes.vo: and instituted Apple's corporate philosophy: empathy with the customer, focus,

scenes.vo: and "imputing"â€”the belief that people judge a book by its cover, and that beautiful design signals quality before the power switch is even flipped.

scenes.label: COMPETITORS' DRAB GREY BOXES

scenes.vo: They were buying it because it calculated corporate financial forecasts in twenty seconds instead of twenty days.

scenes.vo: He became convinced of his absolute infallibility.

scenes.label: OBJECT-ORIENTED CODE

scenes.label: ETHERNET NETWORKING

scenes.vo: and a graphical user interface where a handheld mouse moved a cursor across virtual windows on a screen.

scenes.vo: Jobs stared at the screen, his pupils dilated in pure shock.

scenes.vo: Xerox was a copier company whose corporate executives had zero idea what their scientists had built.

scenes.label: WHY AREN'T YOU DOING THIS?
scenes.vo: Jobs began pacing the room, shouting: "Why aren't you doing anything with this?

scenes.label: THE GREATEST THING
scenes.vo: This is the greatest thing!

scenes.label: THE DIGITAL GOLD MINE
scenes.vo: You are sitting on a gold mine!"

scenes.vo: Jobs raced back to Apple, determined to build the graphical interface into Appleâ€™s next corporate machine: the Lisa.

scenes.vo: It was a disaster.

scenes.label: DAILY SPEC SHIFTS
scenes.vo: Jobs meddled with engineering teams, changed architectural specs daily,

scenes.label: STRATOSPHERIC COSTS
scenes.vo: and drove costs into the stratosphere.

scenes.vo: It flopped catastrophically.

scenes.label: STRIPPED OF LISA AUTHORITY
scenes.vo: Humiliated, the board stripped Jobs of all authority on the Lisa project.

scenes.vo: Furious, Jobs sought revenge.

scenes.label: THE PIRATE FLAG
scenes.vo: He hoisted a black pirate flag with a skull and rainbow Apple eye patch above the Macintosh building

scenes.label: BETTER TO BE PIRATES
scenes.vo: and told his team: "It is better to be a pirate than to join the Navy."

scenes.label: 90-HOUR WEEKS
scenes.vo: The Macintosh engineers worked eighty to ninety hours a week,

scenes.label: WEARING EXHAUSTION
scenes.vo: wearing t-shirts that boasted of their exhaustion.

scenes.label: REALITY DISTORTION FIELD
scenes.vo: Jobs pushed them through what colleagues called his "Reality Distortion Field"â€”

scenes.label: CHARM & ABUSE
scenes.vo: a hypnotic blend of charismatic charm, relentless will, and psychological abuse.

scenes.label: THIS IS GARBAGE
scenes.vo: If an engineer presented code Jobs didn't like, he would scream that it was garbage.

scenes.label: THE STOLEN EUREKA
scenes.vo: If an engineer solved an impossible problem, Jobs would return two days later and claim the idea as his own.

scenes.label: THE DEVOTED TEAM
scenes.vo: Yet they worshipped him.

scenes.label: THE IMPOSSIBLE ACHIEVED
scenes.vo: Because he forced them to achieve engineering feats they did not believe were possible.

scenes.label: CHAMPAGNE, FEB 10 1982
scenes.vo: On February 10, 1982, Jobs brought the entire team together with a bottle of champagne,

scenes.label: REAL ARTISTS SIGN
scenes.vo: "Real artists sign their work," Jobs proclaimed.

scenes.vo: To launch the computer, Jobs demanded an advertising earthquake.

scenes.label: RIDLEY SCOTT ON SET
scenes.vo: He hired Hollywood director Ridley Scott

scenes.vo: Suddenly, a lone female athlete in bright red shorts sprints down the aisle

scenes.vo: and hurls a sledgehammer through the screen, exploding it in a shower of sparks and blinding light.

scenes.label: BOARDROOM HORROR
scenes.vo: Appleâ€™s board of directors watched a screening in horror.

scenes.vo: They thought it was reckless, arrogant, and humiliating.

scenes.vo: They ordered the advertising agency to sell off the Super Bowl commercial slots.

scenes.vo: Steve Wozniak offered to pay for half the broadcast out of his own pocket.

scenes.vo: It aired only once on national television, but it dominated every evening news broadcast in America.

scenes.vo: He wore a polka-dot bow tie.

scenes.vo: It sure is great to get out of that bag...

scenes.label: CANNOT LIFT

scenes.label: TEARS IN THE FRONT ROW
scenes.vo: People in the front rows were weeping.

scenes.vo: Then, the cold reality hit.

scenes.vo: The Macintosh was visually breathtaking, but technologically crippled.

scenes.vo: The company was hemorrhaging tens of millions of dollars.

scenes.vo: Tensions between Jobs and CEO John Sculley erupted into toxic hostility.

scenes.vo: Jobs had lured Sculley from Pepsi in 1983 with his famous, stinging challenge:

scenes.vo: Now, Sculley found himself managing an erratic, vindictive founder whose division was threatening to bankrupt the entire corporation.

scenes.vo: In May 1985, while Sculley was scheduled to be in China on a trade mission, Jobs plotted a palace coup to remove him and seize control of Apple.

scenes.label: THE WHISPERED WARNING
scenes.vo: An executive warned Sculley.

scenes.label: THE BOARDROOM SHOWDOWN

scenes.vo: He polled the board of directors one by one: "Do you back Steve, or do you back me?"

scenes.label: THE UNANIMOUS BACKING
scenes.vo: Every single board member voted for Sculley.

scenes.label: STRIPPED OF ALL POWER
scenes.vo: Steve Jobs was stripped of all operational responsibility.

scenes.label: BANISHED TO SIBERIA
scenes.vo: He was banished to an empty office in an auxiliary building that employees mockingly nicknamed "Siberia."

scenes.label: THE SILENT TELEPHONE
scenes.vo: His phone stopped ringing. Nobody came to his office.

scenes.label: SEPTEMBER 17, 1985
scenes.vo: On September 17, 1985, Steve Jobs resigned from Apple.

scenes.label: SELLING EVERY SHARE
scenes.vo: In a fit of bitter fury, he sold every single share of his Apple stockâ€”millions of shares worth over one hundred million dollarsâ€”

scenes.label: THE ONE REMAINING SHARE
scenes.vo: retaining only one single share so he would still receive the annual shareholder reports in the mail.

scenes.label: THIRTY YEARS OLD
scenes.vo: He was thirty years old.

scenes.label: THE EXILED MILLIONAIRE
scenes.vo: He was a multi-millionaire.

scenes.label: COMPLETELY FINISHED
scenes.vo: And in the eyes of Silicon Valley, he was completely finished.

scenes.label: THE 11-YEAR WILDERNESS
scenes.vo: What followed was a brutal eleven-year wilderness.

scenes.label: PRIDE RESURGENT
scenes.vo: But his pride would not let him stay down.

scenes.label: $7M PERSONAL STAKE
